(1) the expression of the alternatively-spliced isoforms of type A γ-amine butyric acid (GABA) receptor β2 (β2L and β2S) subunit is significantly reduced in the postmortem brains of schizophrenia; (2) the heterozygotes of rs1876072 and rs2546620, and homozygotes of rs2546622 and rs1876071, are correlated with reduced expression levels of β2 subunit;

a genetic mechanism that may underlie the etiology of schizophrenia and the functional consequences of the genetic mechanism.

the expression and electrogphysiological properties of the alternatively spiced isoforms of GABA(A) receptor beta2 subunit, which may provide an insight into the pathogenesis mechanism for schizophrenia.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GABRB2 is a schizophrenia susceptibility gene.

the expression levels of the GABAA receptor beta2 subunit are significantly reduced in schizophrenia and that this reduction is genotype-dependent, and this reduction is associated with the electrophysiological changes in GABAergic transmission.
the two isoforms of β2 have different expression and functional properties, and that the expression of the two isoform genes is associated with schizophrenia and with specific genotypes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GABA(A)R β2 subunit is a promising schizophrenia susceptibility gene, and the GABA(A)-related mechanisms may contribute to the pathogenesis of the disease.
the two isoforms of GABA receptor β2 subunits have differential electrophysiological and expression properties.
GABRB2 gene is involved in the etiopathogenesis of schizophrenia, which could be mediated by the expression of the alternatively-spliced isoforms of the GABAA receptor subunit β2.

there is a differential expression of the two isoform of GABAA β2 receptor, which has different electrophysiology properties and may play a role in schizophrenia.

the two isoforms of GABAAR β2 subunit are differentially expressed in the postmortem brain of patients with schizophrenia, and that the expression of these isoforms is influenced by the GABRB2 polymorphisms in a genotype-specific manner.
